relationships.relation_statement: For the same n in {2,3,4,5}, set each symmetric off-diagonal edge coupling to k_i*k_j, absorbing any common 1/n normalization. The phase equations are then exactly rank-one Kuramoto equations with the same reference phase and frequency constraint.
relationships.evidence_location: Section 1, equations (2)–(5); Section 2, IC1 and phase-shift quotient.
relationships.inheritance_policy: Input inclusion only; generic complex counts, monodromy and discriminants of arbitrary symmetric couplings do not automatically specialize to the rank-one locus.
relationships.caveats: Coupling diagonal entries do not enter the sine-difference equations. Rank one refers to the full factorized coupling matrix including any chosen diagonal, not the zero-diagonal adjacency matrix.

relationships.relation_statement: Choose the complete graph K_n, n in {2,3,4,5}, and factorized symmetric edge couplings k_i*k_j, with the same phase normalization and frequency constraint.
relationships.evidence_location: Section 1, equations (2)–(5); Section 2, IC1 and phase-shift quotient.
relationships.inheritance_policy: Input inclusion only. No graph-generic or arbitrary-coupling count or monodromy is inherited on the rank-one locus.
relationships.caveats: Take the factors nonzero for full complete-graph support; allow zero factors only as a further degeneracy, not as generic complete-graph data.
